Took a break from hanging planters, made a decorative flower basket for the bay window.
That looks pro! Does the bucket have a drainage tray?

Thanks! There's a little green felt pad around it, but 50% of the pot's contents are drainage substrate. (I didn't take any good photos of that process, sorry)

I took an old plastic mud rug and cut some strips to make a liner for the pot, then added a few rocks and mulch before setting the plants on top.

We'll see if it works properly, but the idea is that the substrate catches any excess water and holds it nearby to keep the soil moist.

• Step One - Buy some flowers from the local nursery. Impatiens, grass, basil, and that weird red-leaved thing. I didn't know their names at the time, I just bought them based on their sun preference (partial to shade) and the basil because I like how it smells.

  • Step Two - An enameled metal pot that we've used before - I lined the bottom with plastic matting, rocks, and mulch for drainage. This is important for any planter, it holds extra moisture for the soil without making it too soggy. Plants are pretty picky about how wet the ground is, apparently.

  • Step Three - Gently remove the plants and arrange them in the planter! They had more than enough soil around them in their pots, although some of them were a little rootbound. The soil didn't seem very good so they may need fertilizer, we'll see.

  • Step Four - Water 'em! This helps the plants recover from transplanting and helps the soil soften so it can settle together. Also a good drainage test for the pot.

  • Step Five - Enjoy your new planter basket! This south-facing window should give them more than enough sun.
